- Engineering excellence and customisation capability, cited by management as underpinning each of its stated opportunities
- EIL approval for On-Off valves with Duncan make actuators - management notes the oil & gas sector's stringent qualification requirements make it difficult to enter, but equally difficult to displace once established
- Aftermarket and dealer network providing recurring replacement and service revenue and rapid access to spares across major industrial hubs
- Balanced mix across aftermarket, project and emerging segments, which management says provides both stability and growth

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Intensifying market competition — The valves, pneumatics and valve automation sector faces fierce competition from both established multinationals and domestic players; management says this competitive intensity drives pricing pressure and demands continuous differentiation in products and services.
- Price sensitivity and margin pressure — Indian industrial customers remain highly price-conscious, especially in large-scale projects. Management says balancing competitive pricing against the need to maintain quality and innovation can challenge profitability, particularly as input costs fluctuate.
- Dependence on customer capital-investment cycles — Demand is closely linked to capex across infrastructure, energy and industrials. Any slowdown in capex sanctions, delays in EPC award timelines, or deferral of large industrial projects can impact business growth - a direct order-flow exposure for a project-linked component supplier.
- Regulatory and compliance complexity in approval-gated sectors — Evolving regulatory standards, certifications and sector-specific approvals - especially in public sector, defence and nuclear projects - can cause delays, raise compliance costs and act as a barrier to market entry for new products. This is the flip side of the qualification moat the Company is trying to build in oil & gas, defence and nuclear.
- Supply chain vulnerability — Global and domestic supply chains are susceptible to disruption from geopolitical tensions, natural calamities, logistics bottlenecks and raw material shortages, which can affect timely production, increase costs and impact customer delivery commitments.
- Technological change and shifting customer expectations — Customer preferences are shifting rapidly toward integrated, digitally enabled and sustainable automation solutions, with demand for customised products, advanced diagnostics and energy-efficient systems; failing to stay agile risks loss of market relevance and long-term partnerships.
- Talent and capability gaps — Attracting and retaining skilled talent in applications engineering, R&D, quality assurance, project management and technical service is described as crucial; a shortage of specialised skills may limit the Company's ability to innovate and execute complex projects. The Board separately flags high employee turnover ratio and labour unrest as factors that may adversely affect performance in the upcoming financial year.
- Macroeconomic and policy uncertainty — Inflation, currency movements, changes in import duty structures and shifts in government spending priorities can each affect demand patterns and cost bases - relevant given the Company's dependence on government-led infrastructure investment and its export ambitions.

outlook.body:
- Penetrate the oil & gas sector on the back of the newly secured Engineers India Limited (EIL) certification for On-Off valves with Duncan make actuators, gradually building presence with end users and EPC contractors in refineries, petrochemicals and pipelines; establishing a track record with marquee clients is described as foundational to longer-term growth there.
- Strengthen the product portfolio through further key certifications and approvals that enable entry into regulated and high-specification sectors.
- Build a position in Knife Gate Valves (KGV) and bulk solid handling applications over the medium term, serving power, cement and steel through both project and replacement demand.
- Expand internationally, particularly in the Middle East, through DEL Arabia - the wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on December 11, 2025 - to enhance local presence, improve customer engagement and diversify revenue streams.
- Foray into defence and nuclear with fluid power systems for mission-critical national projects, supporting India's indigenisation goals; first commercial orders in this vertical have been received.
- Actively track project pipelines in oil & gas, power, cement, steel, metals and infrastructure so that solutions are precisely aligned to industry needs and new business is captured.
- Expand the dealer network and enhance aftermarket services so customers get rapid access to spares, repairs and maintenance across major industrial hubs, minimising downtime and reinforcing customer loyalty.
- Maintain a balanced growth trajectory across aftermarket, project and emerging segments for both stability and growth.
- Invest in people - hiring, training and leadership development - to build the next layer of capability beneath the existing board and management team, described as the operational imperative and crucial to FY2027 outcomes.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Duncan Engineering's expansion in FY2026 was footprint- and portfolio-led rather than a plant capex programme; no new plant, line or capacity addition is described anywhere in this bundle. The single concrete corporate expansion step was geographic: during the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on December 11, 2025 - DEL Arabia - 'inter-alia to carry out the business activities of the Company and for expanding its market presence in the Middle East Region', which management expects to enhance local presence and customer engagement and to diversify revenue streams over the medium term. Product-portfolio expansion is described through certifications rather than capacity: the Company secured Engineers India Limited (EIL) certification for On-Off valves with Duncan make actuators, which it says enables entry into regulated and high-specification sectors such as oil & gas and improves its ability to engage leading EPC contractors and end users. Adjacent expansion themes are an 'expanding product portfolio' in Knife Gate Valves and bulk solid handling for power, cement and steel over the medium term; a foray into defence and nuclear fluid power systems where the Company says it has begun receiving its first commercial orders; and expansion of the dealer network and aftermarket service infrastructure across major industrial hubs. No commissioning dates, ramp timelines or rupee capex quantum are disclosed for any of these.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Increasing adoption of industrial automation across sectors is expected to support long-term demand for valves, pneumatic and valve automation solutions in both project and replacement markets.
- Ongoing investment in infrastructure and core sectors - power, oil & gas, water, metals and cement - is creating sustained demand for flow control and automation products, particularly in new installations and capacity expansions.
- Investments in refining capacity, LNG infrastructure and the emerging green hydrogen ecosystem are creating demand for certified, high-specification flow control; management notes the sector's stringent qualification requirements make it 'difficult to enter, but equally difficult to displace once established'.
- Rising focus on maintenance, uptime and lifecycle efficiency is driving steady demand for replacement products and service-led offerings, providing stability and recurring revenue opportunities.
- India's push for self-reliance in defence and nuclear offers opportunities to supply high-spec pneumatic, hydraulic and valve automation solutions.
- India's reputation as a manufacturing hub plus cost competitiveness is boosting export opportunities in the Middle East, US, Africa and Southeast Asia, offering global revenue diversification.
- Increasing awareness of workplace safety and environmental regulation drives adoption of pneumatic systems and valve automation products meeting those standards.
- Industry mix is shifting from standalone components toward integrated automation packages - actuators, valves, control systems and monitoring working as a single system - a trend management expects to strengthen over coming years.
- The Indian pneumatic and valve automation industry is forecast to grow ~7% CAGR till 2033, driven by industrial growth, infrastructure development and increasing automation.
- Demand is increasingly for customised solutions with strong technical support and faster turnaround, rather than off-the-shelf products - which management frames as playing to Duncan's engineering and customisation strengths.
- Customers are placing more weight on quality, lifecycle cost and service support than on upfront pricing, a gradual shift toward value-driven purchasing.
- Offsetting driver: the market remains highly competitive and price-sensitive, especially in large project businesses, requiring a careful balance between cost competitiveness and product quality.
- Government-led investment in water management, power, cement, steel and transportation, plus 'Make in India' localisation, continues to generate consistent demand and open customers to domestic sourcing.
- Defence and nuclear: 'the company has begun receiving its first commercial orders in this vertical' - no order-book value disclosed.
- Management describes a 'healthy project pipeline' in the Indian market and says it actively monitors project pipelines in oil & gas, power, cement, steel, metals and infrastructure; no quantified order book or backlog is disclosed in this bundle.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Increasing adoption of industrial automation across sectors is expected to support long-term demand for valves, pneumatic and valve automation solutions in both project and replacement markets.
- Ongoing investment in infrastructure and core sectors - power, oil & gas, water, metals and cement - is creating sustained demand for flow control and automation products, particularly in new installations and capacity expansions.
- Investments in refining capacity, LNG infrastructure and the emerging green hydrogen ecosystem are creating demand for certified, high-specification flow control; management notes the sector's stringent qualification requirements make it 'difficult to enter, but equally difficult to displace once established'.
- Rising focus on maintenance, uptime and lifecycle efficiency is driving steady demand for replacement products and service-led offerings, providing stability and recurring revenue opportunities.
- India's push for self-reliance in defence and nuclear offers opportunities to supply high-spec pneumatic, hydraulic and valve automation solutions.
- India's reputation as a manufacturing hub plus cost competitiveness is boosting export opportunities in the Middle East, US, Africa and Southeast Asia, offering global revenue diversification.
- Increasing awareness of workplace safety and environmental regulation drives adoption of pneumatic systems and valve automation products meeting those standards.
- Industry mix is shifting from standalone components toward integrated automation packages - actuators, valves, control systems and monitoring working as a single system - a trend management expects to strengthen over coming years.
- The Indian pneumatic and valve automation industry is forecast to grow ~7% CAGR till 2033, driven by industrial growth, infrastructure development and increasing automation.
- Demand is increasingly for customised solutions with strong technical support and faster turnaround, rather than off-the-shelf products - which management frames as playing to Duncan's engineering and customisation strengths.
- Customers are placing more weight on quality, lifecycle cost and service support than on upfront pricing, a gradual shift toward value-driven purchasing.
- Offsetting driver: the market remains highly competitive and price-sensitive, especially in large project businesses, requiring a careful balance between cost competitiveness and product quality.
- Government-led investment in water management, power, cement, steel and transportation, plus 'Make in India' localisation, continues to generate consistent demand and open customers to domestic sourcing.
- Defence and nuclear: 'the company has begun receiving its first commercial orders in this vertical' - no order-book value disclosed.
- Management describes a 'healthy project pipeline' in the Indian market and says it actively monitors project pipelines in oil & gas, power, cement, steel, metals and infrastructure; no quantified order book or backlog is disclosed in this bundle.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Penetrate the oil & gas sector on the back of the newly secured Engineers India Limited (EIL) certification for On-Off valves with Duncan make actuators, gradually building presence with end users and EPC contractors in refineries, petrochemicals and pipelines; establishing a track record with marquee clients is described as foundational to longer-term growth there.
- Strengthen the product portfolio through further key certifications and approvals that enable entry into regulated and high-specification sectors.
- Build a position in Knife Gate Valves (KGV) and bulk solid handling applications over the medium term, serving power, cement and steel through both project and replacement demand.
- Expand internationally, particularly in the Middle East, through DEL Arabia - the wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on December 11, 2025 - to enhance local presence, improve customer engagement and diversify revenue streams.
- Foray into defence and nuclear with fluid power systems for mission-critical national projects, supporting India's indigenisation goals; first commercial orders in this vertical have been received.
- Actively track project pipelines in oil & gas, power, cement, steel, metals and infrastructure so that solutions are precisely aligned to industry needs and new business is captured.
- Expand the dealer network and enhance aftermarket services so customers get rapid access to spares, repairs and maintenance across major industrial hubs, minimising downtime and reinforcing customer loyalty.
- Maintain a balanced growth trajectory across aftermarket, project and emerging segments for both stability and growth.
- Invest in people - hiring, training and leadership development - to build the next layer of capability beneath the existing board and management team, described as the operational imperative and crucial to FY2027 outcomes.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Duncan Engineering's expansion in FY2026 was footprint- and portfolio-led rather than a plant capex programme; no new plant, line or capacity addition is described anywhere in this bundle. The single concrete corporate expansion step was geographic: during the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on December 11, 2025 - DEL Arabia - 'inter-alia to carry out the business activities of the Company and for expanding its market presence in the Middle East Region', which management expects to enhance local presence and customer engagement and to diversify revenue streams over the medium term. Product-portfolio expansion is described through certifications rather than capacity: the Company secured Engineers India Limited (EIL) certification for On-Off valves with Duncan make actuators, which it says enables entry into regulated and high-specification sectors such as oil & gas and improves its ability to engage leading EPC contractors and end users. Adjacent expansion themes are an 'expanding product portfolio' in Knife Gate Valves and bulk solid handling for power, cement and steel over the medium term; a foray into defence and nuclear fluid power systems where the Company says it has begun receiving its first commercial orders; and expansion of the dealer network and aftermarket service infrastructure across major industrial hubs. No commissioning dates, ramp timelines or rupee capex quantum are disclosed for any of these.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Engineering excellence and customisation capability, cited by management as underpinning each of its stated opportunities
- EIL approval for On-Off valves with Duncan make actuators - management notes the oil & gas sector's stringent qualification requirements make it difficult to enter, but equally difficult to displace once established
- Aftermarket and dealer network providing recurring replacement and service revenue and rapid access to spares across major industrial hubs
- Balanced mix across aftermarket, project and emerging segments, which management says provides both stability and growth
- Experienced board and management team described as providing a strong foundation
- Cordial industrial relations - a 3-year wage revision agreement signed with the recognised workers' union on March 28, 2024 covering April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2027

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Intensifying market competition — The valves, pneumatics and valve automation sector faces fierce competition from both established multinationals and domestic players; management says this competitive intensity drives pricing pressure and demands continuous differentiation in products and services.
- Price sensitivity and margin pressure — Indian industrial customers remain highly price-conscious, especially in large-scale projects. Management says balancing competitive pricing against the need to maintain quality and innovation can challenge profitability, particularly as input costs fluctuate.
- Dependence on customer capital-investment cycles — Demand is closely linked to capex across infrastructure, energy and industrials. Any slowdown in capex sanctions, delays in EPC award timelines, or deferral of large industrial projects can impact business growth - a direct order-flow exposure for a project-linked component supplier.
- Regulatory and compliance complexity in approval-gated sectors — Evolving regulatory standards, certifications and sector-specific approvals - especially in public sector, defence and nuclear projects - can cause delays, raise compliance costs and act as a barrier to market entry for new products. This is the flip side of the qualification moat the Company is trying to build in oil & gas, defence and nuclear.
- Supply chain vulnerability — Global and domestic supply chains are susceptible to disruption from geopolitical tensions, natural calamities, logistics bottlenecks and raw material shortages, which can affect timely production, increase costs and impact customer delivery commitments.
- Technological change and shifting customer expectations — Customer preferences are shifting rapidly toward integrated, digitally enabled and sustainable automation solutions, with demand for customised products, advanced diagnostics and energy-efficient systems; failing to stay agile risks loss of market relevance and long-term partnerships.
- Talent and capability gaps — Attracting and retaining skilled talent in applications engineering, R&D, quality assurance, project management and technical service is described as crucial; a shortage of specialised skills may limit the Company's ability to innovate and execute complex projects. The Board separately flags high employee turnover ratio and labour unrest as factors that may adversely affect performance in the upcoming financial year.
- Macroeconomic and policy uncertainty — Inflation, currency movements, changes in import duty structures and shifts in government spending priorities can each affect demand patterns and cost bases - relevant given the Company's dependence on government-led infrastructure investment and its export ambitions.
